# Allow list of invented account and card identifiers used in this repository.
#
# gate:privacy fails on any account-number or card-number shape anywhere in
# the tree that is not listed here. That is the point. The check is not "is
# there an identifier", because fixtures need identifiers, it is "is this one
# known". A new one stops the gate until a person looks at where it came from.
#
# Nothing on this list may be taken from a real statement. When adding an
# entry, say where you invented it. If you cannot say, it does not go on the
# list.
#
# HOW MATCHING WORKS. Once a value is FOUND, both sides are normalised the
# same way before comparison: spaces and dashes are removed, mask glyphs are
# folded so x and X and * are one value, and letters are upper-cased.
#
# WHAT IS FOUND is three separate patterns, and they do not cover the same
# ground. Stated one by one because this paragraph has now been wrong in
# both directions (fix round 4 finding CR3-M3P3-02, fix round 5 findings
# HZ4-M3P3-02 and CR4-M3P3-01): first it under-promised, then it replaced
# that with "case-insensitively and accept letters in the body", which is
# true of one pattern each and of neither on its own.
#
#   LOCAL account shape: two letters, two digits, then twelve DIGITS in
#   groups of four, separated by spaces or not. Either case. This is the
#   Belgian-length shape and it is the only one that tolerates separators.
#
#   FOREIGN account shape: two letters, two digits, then ten to thirty
#   letters-or-digits, COMPACT only, either case. This is what reaches an
#   account number whose body carries letters. It takes no separators on
#   purpose: allowing them inside a variable-length body made the match run
#   past the account number into the following word and invented shapes
#   nobody could write a provenance note for, measured in fix round 4.
#
#   CARD shapes: sixteen digits in four groups, and the masked form, both
#   with separators and either case.
#
# SO WHAT NEITHER ACCOUNT PATTERN COVERS, said plainly: an account number
# whose body carries letters AND is written with spaces or hyphens is found
# by nothing here. The local pattern refuses the letters and the foreign one
# refuses the separators. Nothing in the tree is written that way today and
# every value that is, is listed; a future fixture that writes one would go
# unchecked, and closing it means giving the foreign shape a separator rule
# that cannot run past the value.
#
# Binary and lockfile paths are skipped, because grep reads no text in them;
# a committed PDF is scanned, and rule 3 of the script refuses a compressed
# one for that reason.

# --- accounts -------------------------------------------------------------

# The IBAN example from the Wikipedia IBAN article, and a digit-shuffled
# variant. The household's current account across the unit, property and e2e
# fixtures.
BE68539007547034
BE68539075417034

# Second and third invented accounts, wherever a fixture needs a pot or a
# counterparty account distinct from the current account.
#
# THE FIRST OF THE TWO WAS REPLACED IN M3-P14 and the old value is gone from
# the tree. It was BE + two check digits + the run 539007547099, and those
# check digits did not satisfy ISO 7064, which did not matter while an
# account could only be declared from the file that introduced it. From
# M3-P14 the household TYPES every account number at setup and a number
# failing the check is refused, so a fixture whose own account fails the
# check can no longer be registered at all. The body is unchanged; only the
# two check digits were recomputed for it.
BE59539007547099
BE02233445566778

# Counterparty accounts in the interpretation and merchant tests. Bank codes
# are real Belgian prefixes, account bodies are the run 123456 continued.
BE71096123456769
BE54540123456789
BE39103123456719
BE43068999999501

# Transfer counterparty in the pairing and merchant tests.
BE02979245566602

# Belfius PDF fixture accounts, emitted by the fixture builder at
# test/fixtures/generate-pdf-fixtures.ts. Bodies are sequential runs.
#
# THE FIRST OF THESE IS THE STATEMENT'S OWN ACCOUNT and was recomputed in
# M3-P14 for the same reason as the entry above: from that phase the
# household registers it by typing it, and registration refuses a number
# that fails the ISO 7064 check. The body is the same sequential run; only
# the two check digits changed. The old value is gone from the tree.
BE72012345678944
BE45678901234515
BE77123456789012
BE10987654321001

# Accounts in the original design prototype at
# design/reference/pulse-prototype.html. Constructed by typing a BE, two
# check digits and twelve digits by hand until the shape read like an
# account number; neither validates under the IBAN mod-97 check, which is
# positive evidence they were made up rather than copied. Provenance note
# added in fix round 2 (finding CR-M3P3-06): the note here used to say
# where they are USED, and this file's own rule at the top asks where they
# were INVENTED, which is the one thing it did not say.
BE71479602578213
BE68973942180011

# Documented placeholder. Deliberately not a valid IBAN: check digits 00
# never validate. Used in the mobile mockup under delivery/design/.
BE00000000000000

# --- accounts whose body carries letters -----------------------------------
# Surfaced in fix round 4 (finding HZ3-M3P3-03) when the account pattern was
# widened to accept letters in the body: until then no pattern here matched a
# non-Belgian account number at all, and these had been sitting in tracked
# fixtures with the gate exiting 0.
#
# All three are the PUBLISHED WORKED EXAMPLES from the IBAN specification's
# own documentation, the same source the first entry in this file names, used
# by the generic delimited fixtures to exercise a non-Belgian counterparty
# column. None was transcribed from anything: each was copied from public
# specification text, and each was probed against every real statement in the
# container and returns zero hits.
DE89370400440532013000
FR1420041010050500013M02606
NL91ABNA0417164300

# --- card numbers ---------------------------------------------------------
# Present so the masking work in M3-P6 has something to mask. None is a live
# PAN: each is a test prefix or a visible pattern.

# The 4000 test-card prefix continued with the run 123456789010, in the M3-P6
# masking fixtures and work history.
4000123456789010
4000-1234-5678-9010

# Straight digit runs, used where the fixture only needs a card shape.
1234567890123456
9999999999999999

# Patterned invented PANs in the Belfius PDF fixtures and the M3-P6 notes.
5599208877665544
5390754170349210

# Masked forms of the two invented PANs above. A card statement prints only
# the masked form, so the gate must know these as well as the bare digits.
400012XXXXXX9010
559920XXXXXX5544

# The two cards of the KBC PDF fixtures, in the masked form a card
# statement prints (test/fixtures/generate-pdf-fixtures.ts and the KBC
# fixture PDFs built from it). Invented the same way as the patterned PANs
# above: a Mastercard-shaped six-digit head, the mask glyphs the layout
# itself prints, and a hand-picked four-digit tail, one descending and one
# ascending so the pair reads as made up at a glance. The second exists so
# a fixture can carry a SECOND card of the same issuer, which is what the
# two-cards-one-account finding needed to be witnessed.
#
# Checked before listing, not asserted: each was probed against every real
# statement present in the container at fix-round-2 review time, in its
# masked form, its six-digit head and its four-digit tail, and returned
# zero WHOLE-TOKEN hits in all three forms in both documents. QUALIFIED IN
# FIX ROUND 4 (finding CR3-M3P3-03), because the unqualified sentence was
# true under a token reading and false under a plain one: a four-digit tail
# is four digits, and four digits turn up inside longer unrelated reference
# runs. What was checked, and what matters, is that no probe occurs as a
# value in its own right. That is the only check available to anyone here,
# and it is the one that would have caught a transcription.
541788XXXXXX3210
541788XXXXXX7654

# The third card, added in fix round 3 for the credit-balance statement
# fixture, so that family keeps one card per document and the identity
# witnesses stay unambiguous. Invented and probed the same way as the two
# above: masked form, six-digit head and four-digit tail, zero hits in all
# three forms against every real statement in the container.
541788XXXXXX9081

# The fourth card, added in fix round 4 for the underpaid statement
# fixture. Same construction and the same three-form check as the three
# above.
541788XXXXXX6503

# --- M3-P12 counterparty-identity fixture ---------------------------------
# Emitted by test/fixtures/generate-pdf-fixtures.ts into
# belfius-counterparty-identity.pdf. Every value here was constructed by
# hand for this fixture and none was transcribed from anything.
#
# HOW THEY WERE INVENTED: the twelve-digit body of each is a run of repeated
# digit pairs typed in ascending order (1111 2222 3333, then 2222 3333 4444,
# and so on), which reads as made up at a glance, and the two ISO 7064 check
# digits were then COMPUTED for that body so the value passes the trust gate
# this phase adds. A fixture whose accounts all failed the gate could not
# witness the account basis at all: every committed fixture that predates
# this phase carries accounts that fail mod-97, measured, which is why new
# ones were needed rather than reused.
BE31111122223333
BE78222233334444
BE28333344445555
BE75444455556666
BE25555566667777
BE72666677778888

# The two longer-than-Belgian sources that witness the truncation hazard.
# Built the same way: the body is a typed run, both carry the SAME computed
# check digits, and they differ only in their last three digits, which is
# what makes the sixteen-character value the shipped scrape stores identical
# for both. That identical stored value is the third entry, listed because
# the gate finds it in its own right wherever the spaced form appears.
FR0230006000011234567890066
FR0230006000011234567890163
FR02300060000112

# --- M3-P12 fix round: the PAN-shaped view of the two long sources --------
# NOT A NEW VALUE. It is the SAME invented digits already listed above, seen
# through the gate's other pattern. The two FR sources are written spaced in
# the fixture, so the gate's card pattern (four groups of four digits) can
# match the four groups that follow the country code and the check digits,
# yielding this value, while the IBAN pattern matches the country-prefixed
# form and yields FR02300060000112. Which of the two alternatives fires is a
# property of the regex engine's start position, not of the tree, and only
# the IBAN form was listed. The hazard lane of M3-P12 recorded ONE run of
# gate:privacy reporting test/fixtures/baseline-descriptor-keys.json as
# carrying an identifier shape not on the allow list, followed by
# twenty-three clean runs on the identical tree, and this is the only value
# in the whole tree that the card pattern can produce and the list does not
# carry: every other one is listed. Listing it makes the gate's answer the
# same whichever alternative matches. The digits' provenance is the entry for
# the two FR sources above: typed runs, invented, with computed check digits.
3000600001123456

# --- M3-P14 setup fixture accounts -----------------------------------------
# The eight accounts of the owner's own scenario, registered at setup by
# test/e2e/accounts.spec.ts and carried by test/fixtures/setup-current.csv:
# one current account, three further spending accounts and four savings
# accounts.
#
# HOW THEY WERE INVENTED: the twelve-digit body of each is a 9 followed by
# ten zeroes and the account's ordinal, 900000000001 through 900000000008,
# which reads as made up at a glance and cannot be mistaken for a bank's
# real numbering. The two check digits were then COMPUTED for each body so
# every one passes the validity test the setup screen applies; a fixture
# account that failed it could not be registered at all, and every account
# number committed before this phase was measured against that test with 11
# of the 24 distinct values in the tree failing it, which is why new ones
# were needed rather than reused.
#
# The counterparty accounts of the three OUTSIDE merchants in that fixture
# are not new: they are BE71096123456769 and BE39103123456719, already
# listed above, plus one row that carries no counterparty account at all.
BE73900000000001
BE46900000000002
BE19900000000003
BE89900000000004
BE62900000000005
BE35900000000006
BE08900000000007
BE78900000000008

# --- M3-P14 deliberately INVALID probes -----------------------------------
# The four refusals criterion 14.3 requires are asserted over values that
# must FAIL the validity test, so none of these can be a well-formed account
# number and none could ever match anything. Each is derived by hand from
# BE73900000000001 above, whose provenance is the entry for the setup
# accounts, by breaking exactly one of the four tests:
#
#   ZZ73900000000001   the country code replaced by ZZ, which the pinned
#                      ISO 13616 table does not carry.
#   BE7390000000000    one digit short of the length the table assigns BE.
#   BE739000000000012  one digit long.
#   BE73900000000010   the last two digits transposed, so the country and the
#                      length are right and the ISO 7064 check fails. This is
#                      the mistake the criterion is about: one character
#                      wrong by hand.
#   BE46900000000020   the same transposition applied to BE46900000000002,
#                      used by the Playwright test that types three rows and
#                      corrects the one that is refused.
ZZ73900000000001
BE7390000000000
BE739000000000012
BE73900000000010
BE46900000000020

# Probe counterparty invented by the M3-P14 clean-room reviews; appears only

# delivery/review/m3-p14-hazard-round2.yaml, never in a fixture.
BE24902200001138
